correctness.rationale: The reset sign process flips at independent thinned Poisson rate eta*r in addition to intrinsic gamma; future sign correlations decay with beta=2(gamma+eta*r). I independently derived M=E[Xsigma] from the jump generator: M'=v-(2gamma+r)M+r(1-2eta)J/t, J'=M-beta*J, J(0)=0. The boundedness argument gives J=O(1) and M=v/(2gamma+r)+O(t^-1). For V=E[X^2], V'=2vM-rV+r H/t, H'=V. With Y=H/t the exact quadrature Y'=e^{-rt} t^{-2} integral_0^t s e^{rs}(2vM(s))ds yields Y'=2v^2/[r(2gamma+r)t]+O(t^-2), and integrating gives the log law and finite C_eta. Independent one-reset event integrals yield -7r/18 for unchanged sign, -13r/18 for reversed sign; the single intrinsic tumble gives -2gamma/3. Thus the t^3 coefficient, invertible parameter formulas and eta independence are exact. A new numerical integration of the moment equations at eta=0,.25,.5,.75,1 and exact rational one-event checks corroborated the derivation. The all-t asymptotic follows from the integral equation, not numerics.

value.rationale: The theorem distinguishes a physically motivated reset protocol from history-state copying, showing a nontrivial universality of the dominant logarithmic spreading despite eta-dependent transient variance. It also derives exact population-moment identifiability of three kinetic parameters, supplying a concrete reason for the subleading short-time calculation.

limitations: Exact population moments, not a central limit theorem, pathwise spreading theorem, finite-data statistical guarantees or first-passage distribution.
Initial fair sign, v,gamma,r>0 and fixed parameters; the eta identification assumes ideal t-to-zero and asymptotic observations.
The reset velocity is the current velocity possibly flipped; no history-sign copying.
